rules.reason: a shipment is the operator's own paperwork about their own goods; no delete, because a parcel that went out cannot be made not to have gone out -- a mistake is a lost/returned status or an inbound shipment, never a vanished row
the lines are the shipment; same scope and the same no-delete posture, and the over-shipping gate in hook_shipment_lines runs on this path whoever the caller is
packing is warehouse work, not owner-only work: anybody signed in can raise a shipment, and everything they can put in it is bounded by what the order already committed to

operator-facing, deliberately NOT public: the slip is addressed by an internal shipment id, so a public page here would be an enumeration oracle for every parcel in the shop. The customer's door is the payment portal's capability token, which is unguessable and revocable; a slip is printed by the person holding the box
the picker has to be signed in for the page to know whose warehouse to fold; the page itself shows a sign-in prompt rather than an error to anyone who is not

same gate as the pick list and for the same reason: the page folds the signed-in operator's own dock, and it shows a sign-in prompt rather than an error to anybody else. Deliberately not public even though a driver reads it -- the paper in their hand is the copy they get, and a public URL listing every parcel, its destination and its tracking number would be a delivery-route map for anyone who guessed the date

buying postage is bench work, not owner-only work, and it is bounded on every side: it writes nothing but a tracking number and a label file onto one existing shipment, it refuses a parcel whose journey is already over, and with no carrier configured it can only record what an operator typed. The money a real carrier adapter can spend is bounded by that adapter's own credentials, which a signed-in packer does not hold

the scheduler runs this hourly, and an operator watching a parcel should be able to poke it in between without an admin token: it only writes back what the carrier said, and the one derived move it makes (delivered) is the move the carrier just reported
